name: spec
description: Grill scope and acceptance criteria, output a spec file. Use when starting a feature or requirements are vague.

steps.name: Read project context
steps.instruction: Read project context. Check if a recently grilled doc exists for this topic (from /grill-with-docs). If found and still current, skip the grill step - reuse the grilled doc as input.
checklist: Checked for recent grilled doc on this topic

steps.name: Grill requirements
steps.instruction: Follow process/requirements.md. Grill scope, acceptance criteria, and trade-offs. Check SCOPE.md for scope protection rules - never recommend cutting features or endpoints without explicit user approval. Every acceptance criterion must be testable. Enumerate test dimensions from test-selection.json for each acceptance criterion. Mark relevant dimensions and classify each (boundary, equivalence, invariant, transition, environmental). Mark irrelevant dimensions with reasons. For architecture decisions, apply constraint-sheet dimensions.
checklist: Scope grilled - what's in, out, uncertain
Acceptance criteria defined - each is testable
Scope protection checked - no features cut without user approval
Test dimensions enumerated per acceptance criterion
Each dimension classified or marked irrelevant with reason
Key test permutations identified (risk-to-test mapping applied)
Architecture-relevant criteria grounded against constraint sheet

steps.name: Check output location
steps.instruction: Check for J1-type rules (code-as-documentation, no spec files outside ADRs). If active: spec output goes to issue tracker (Linear/GitHub), not docs/specs/. If no J1 rule: write to docs/specs/ as normal.
checklist: Output location decided (issue tracker or docs/specs/)

steps.name: Write spec
steps.instruction: Write the spec to the decided location. Update shared artifacts: GLOSSARY.md if new terms resolved, SCOPE.md if scope changed, CONVENTIONS.md if new patterns emerged. Do not create docs just to cascade into them.

tone: Thorough. Every acceptance criterion is testable. No vague requirements.
